chunks: From him, from Salih, from Al-Hajjaal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever is slain unjustly, We have given to his heir authority, so let him not exceed the limits in slaying.'
He said: 'It was revealed regarding Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Even if all the people of the earth were killed for it, it would not be excessive.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the verse 'And whoever is slain unjustly' regarding Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the verse 'And for the one whose property was taken, We have given his heir authority' (17:33) as specifically revealed in the context of Imam Al-Husayn’s martyrdom. He elucidates that the constraint against 'excess' (*la yusrif*) is relative to the magnitude of the injustice; thus, the killing of all humanity in retribution for Al-Husayn would not constitute excess, highlighting the unparalleled status of his sacrifice in Shia theology.

en.hubeali: H 14812 – From him, from Salih, from Al-Hajjaal, from one of his companions, who has reported:

I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Statement of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic: “[17:33] and whoever is slain unjustly, We have indeed given to his heir authority, so let him not exceed the just limits in slaying”.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It was Revealed regarding Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. Even if all the people of the earth were to be killed for it, it would not be excessive’.
